value.text:
The University of Tokyo (東京大学, Tōkyō Daigaku), also known as UTokyo or Tōdai, is a public research university based in Bunkyō, Tokyo, Japan. Its principal sites are the Hongō, Komaba and Kashiwa campuses, with additional specialised facilities including Shirokanedai. Hongō has served as an administrative centre since 1884; Komaba provides much of the initial undergraduate general education, while Kashiwa is especially associated with graduate study and research. The university is organised into ten faculties and fifteen graduate schools, alongside affiliated research institutes.

The institution was chartered by the Meiji government on 12 April 1877, bringing together earlier schools in law, science, letters and medicine. Its much older educational antecedents include the Shogunate-era Senseiden and astronomical Tenmongata; those were separate institutions, not earlier legal names of the 1877 university. It was renamed Imperial University in 1886 and Tokyo Imperial University in 1897. The name University of Tokyo was restored in 1947, and post-war reforms brought two higher schools into the university in 1949.

Teaching and research span the humanities, law, economics, medicine, engineering, agriculture and natural sciences. The university's research infrastructure includes specialised institutes and a medical teaching hospital. Its recorded student totals vary by measurement date and source: Wikidata reports 28,918 students on 1 May 2025, while a separate encyclopaedic account reports 28,133 for 2022. Financial figures also require period care: the institution's 2022 April budget observation is 281.788 billion yen, while an account of 2021–2022 reports 264.1 billion yen in income. These amounts describe different measures and should not be treated as interchangeable.
